venues.name: Cali Mykonos
venues.note: The island's most talked-about newer address, a serene stone-and-marble retreat on Mykonos's calmer side, built for privacy rather than the party.
credentials: MICHELIN Guide Hotel, Mykonos selection
WELL Certified, Gold (health & wellbeing building standard)
Condé Nast Traveller, featured; 'one of the most luxurious hotels in the Cyclades'

venues.name: Belvedere Mykonos
venues.area: Chora (School of Fine Arts district, above town)
venues.note: The cosmopolitan heart of Mykonos glamour, a sun-bleached Cycladic labyrinth walking distance from town, home to the island's landmark Matsuhisa restaurant and a Six Senses spa.
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World
MICHELIN Guide Hotel, Mykonos selection
Home to Matsuhisa Mykonos (Nobu Matsuhisa) and Six Senses Spa

venues.name: Santa Marina, a Luxury Collection Resort
venues.note: A full private-peninsula resort on Ornos Bay with its own curve of sand, Marriott's Luxury Collection flagship on the island, and home to Jason Atherton's Mykonos Social.
credentials: The Luxury Collection (Marriott)
MICHELIN Guide Hotel, Mykonos selection
Home to Mykonos Social by Jason Atherton and Buddha-Bar Beach

venues.name: Katikies Mykonos
venues.note: An adults-only cliffside hideaway above Agios Ioannis beach, facing the island's best sunsets, all-white, serene, and almost every suite with its own plunge pool or jetted tub.
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World
MICHELIN Guide Hotel, Mykonos selection

venues.name: Kalesma Mykonos
venues.note: A hilltop village of Cycladic suites and villas overlooking the Aegean, nothing smaller than a one-bedroom suite, each with its own heated infinity pool. One of Greece's first MICHELIN Key hotels.
credentials: MICHELIN One Key (2025), inaugural Greece selection
Home to Pere Ubu fine dining

venues.name: Bill&Coo Mykonos
venues.note: An intimate, adults-only design hotel on the water at Megali Ammos, a short walk from town, polished, romantic, and known for one of the island's more serious kitchens.
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World
MICHELIN Guide Hotel, Mykonos selection

venues.name: Cavo Tagoo Mykonos
venues.note: The island's original design landmark, carved white into the cliff above the sea just north of Chora, with a saltwater infinity pool and Kiku, its long-running Japanese restaurant.
credentials: Design Hotels member
MICHELIN Guide Hotel, Mykonos selection
Home to Kiku (Japanese)

venues.name: Mykonos Blu, a Grecotel Resort
venues.note: A Cycladic resort strung above glamorous Psarou beach, bungalows and villas cascading to the sand, steps from the island's most famous beach-club stretch.
credentials: Grecotel, Exclusive Resort
MICHELIN Guide Hotel, Mykonos selection

venues.name: Kensho Ornos
venues.note: A boutique house of understated, natural-material luxury above Ornos Bay, small, design-forward and calm, with a rooftop restaurant over the water.
credentials: MICHELIN Guide Hotel, Mykonos selection
BIG SEE Design Award, architecture & interiors

venues.name: Matsuhisa Mykonos
venues.note: Nobu Matsuhisa's Mykonos table at the Belvedere, the island's landmark restaurant for two decades, and the world's original poolside Matsuhisa, serving the signature black cod miso and new-style sashimi.
credentials: Nobu Matsuhisa (global restaurant group)
At Belvedere Mykonos, The Leading Hotels of the World

venues.name: Pere Ubu at Kalesma
venues.note: The hilltop dining room at Kalesma, refined Cycladic-Mediterranean cooking with produce-led menus, on a terrace with one of the island's finest Aegean panoramas.
credentials: At Kalesma Mykonos, MICHELIN One Key (2025)

venues.name: Interni Restaurant
venues.note: A secret-garden institution in the heart of Chora since 2000, refined Mediterranean cooking, serious cocktails and the island's original dinner-into-party evening.
credentials: Long-running Chora landmark (est. 2000), the original dinner-to-party destination in Mykonos Town

venues.name: Beefbar Mykonos
venues.note: The Mykonos outpost of the international Beefbar group, premium cuts and world grills on a beachfront terrace at Agios Ioannis, run by the Giraudi family.
credentials: Beefbar (international restaurant group, founded Monte-Carlo)
At Bill&Coo The Coast, Agios Ioannis bay

venues.name: M-eating
venues.note: Chef Panagiotis Menardos's contemporary take on Cycladic and Greek recipes, in a restored early-1900s townhouse in the heart of town, the island's most respected Greek fine-dining room.
credentials: Greek Gastronomy Guide, featured
Long-established Chora fine-dining landmark

venues.name: Bakalo
venues.note: A warm, unpretentious Greek eatery in the Lakka quarter of old town, honest regional recipes done well, long a favourite of visiting names for its lack of fuss.
credentials: Established Chora favourite (est. 2010); expanded internationally (Miami Beach outpost)

venues.name: Kastro's
venues.note: On the water's edge in 18th-century Little Venice since 1976, one of the most photographed rooms on the island, its balcony tables set between old stone walls and the splashing Aegean.
credentials: Little Venice landmark since 1976, among the island's most established and photographed tables

venues.name: Kadena
venues.note: An all-day room on the Gialos waterfront in town, Mediterranean cooking of pasta, seafood and grills with the harbour and fishing boats in view.
credentials: Established waterfront restaurant on Gialos, Mykonos Town

venues.name: Alemagou
venues.note: A bohemian beach taverna on windswept Ftelia, Aegean-fusion cooking, a serious wine list and a laid-back, barefoot afternoon-into-evening mood far from the glossy clubs.
credentials: Star Wine List, recognised wine programme
Long-running Ftelia beach institution

venues.name: Mykonos Town (Chora)
venues.note: The whitewashed labyrinth of Mykonos, bougainvillea-draped lanes deliberately built to confuse pirates, now lined with boutiques, cafes and blue-shuttered doorways at every turn. Wander with no map; late afternoon light and early morning (before the cruise crowds) are the honeymoon-photo hours.

venues.name: Little Venice (Alefkandra)
venues.note: A row of 18th-century sea-captains' houses with wooden balconies leaning straight over the Aegean, so the waves lap at the walls. The most romantic sundowner in Mykonos, book a waterfront table and let the sky change colour with a glass in hand.

venues.name: The Windmills of Kato Mili
venues.note: Five white 16th-century windmills on the hill above Little Venice, the single most iconic image of Mykonos, catching the meltemi winds that once ground the island's grain. Time it for sunset when the whole ridge glows gold.

venues.name: Panagia Paraportiani Church
venues.note: A sculptural white cluster of five chapels melted into one form, begun in the 15th century, one of the most photographed churches in all Greece. Pure Cycladic minimalism; catch it against a blue sky or the last pink of dusk.

venues.name: Aegean Maritime Museum
venues.note: A quiet, beautifully-kept museum of Greek seafaring in a traditional Chora mansion, with model ships, old maps and a leafy garden holding the restored 19th-century lantern of the Armenistis lighthouse. A cool, cultured half-hour away from the sun and the crowds.

venues.name: Lena's House
venues.note: A perfectly preserved 19th-century middle-class Mykonian home, furniture, embroidery, framed photographs and all, kept exactly as it was lived in. A small, intimate window into island life before the glamour, right beside the Maritime Museum.

venues.name: Matoyianni Street
venues.note: The main artery of Chora and the island's luxury shopping spine, Louis Vuitton, Dior and Greek designers between the whitewashed walls, alive until well past midnight. The place to see and be seen while browsing.

venues.name: Rarity Gallery
venues.note: Greece's leading contemporary art gallery since 1994, on Kalogera Street, showing international names and hyperrealist sculpture that stops passers-by in their tracks. A serious, collectable stop for art-minded travellers between beach and dinner.

venues.name: Dio Horia Gallery
venues.note: A three-floor contemporary art platform in a converted Mykonian house, with an atmospheric rooftop bar looking over the town's rooftops. Cutting-edge exhibitions and a cocktail with a view, in one address.

venues.name: Panagia Tourliani Monastery
venues.note: The island's most important monastery, founded in 1542 in the inland village of Ano Mera, with a spectacular gilded Baroque altarpiece carved by Florentine artists in 1775. A serene, devotional counterpoint to the coast, and a genuine glimpse of local faith.

venues.name: Ano Mera Village
venues.note: The one real inland village on Mykonos, a tree-shaded square with tavernas serving unhurried, authentic island cooking, far from the port glamour. Where families and multi-gen groups go for a slow, honest Greek lunch.

venues.name: Armenistis Lighthouse
venues.note: An 1891 stone lighthouse on the island's north-western tip, built after a shipwreck, looking across the strait to Tinos. One of the least-crowded, most cinematic sunset perches on Mykonos, pack a picnic and arrive early.

venues.name: 180° Sunset Bar
venues.note: Perched on the walls of the old Castle Panigirakis at the highest point above town, this bar delivers the full panoramic sweep over Chora, the windmills and the sea as the sun drops. A polished spot for a celebratory sundown cocktail.

venues.name: Caprice Bar, Little Venice
venues.note: The classic waterfront sunset bar of Little Venice, where the Aegean laps at the terrace and the whole crowd turns to watch the sky. Get there before sunset to claim a table right at the water's edge.

venues.name: Psarou Beach
venues.note: The glamour beach of Mykonos, a sheltered golden crescent of turquoise water fronted by Nammos, where yachts anchor offshore and the jet-set sunbathe. Chic, family-friendly and firmly see-and-be-seen; book a lounger well ahead in season.

venues.name: Ornos Beach
venues.note: The most family-friendly beach on the island, a calm, shallow south-coast bay with good hotels, restaurants and water taxis at its doorstep. Easygoing and central, ideal for multi-generation trips with young children.

venues.name: Platis Gialos Beach
venues.note: The best all-round beach on Mykonos, a long stretch of golden sand, clear water and a good range of tavernas and beach bars, plus the hub for the south-coast water taxi that hops between every beach. Wonderfully practical for a full, easy beach day.

venues.name: Paradise Beach
venues.note: The legendary party beach, golden sand by day that turns into open-air dance floors as the sun sets, home to the famous Cavo Paradiso club on the cliff above. Framed here as the scene: go for the spectacle, or skip it if you want quiet.

venues.name: Super Paradise Beach
venues.note: The other half of the party legend, a stunning cove with brilliant water, beach clubs and daytime dancing that runs late into the afternoon. Iconic, hedonistic and inclusive; best appreciated by those who want the full Mykonos energy.

venues.name: Elia Beach
venues.note: The longest and most sophisticated of the organised south-coast beaches, broad, sandy, with space to breathe, good clubs and watersports at one end. A smart choice for a relaxed but well-serviced beach day.

venues.name: Kalo Livadi Beach
venues.note: Golden sand and clear water without the south-coast party machine, longer than Psarou, less crowded than Platis Gialos, with excellent beachfront restaurants. The sweet spot for couples and families who want style without the crush.

venues.name: Agios Sostis Beach
venues.note: A completely undeveloped north-coast beach, no sunbeds, no bars, no buses, just raw Cycladic coastline reached on foot. For a day of true privacy, with Kiki's Tavern hidden on the hill above for lunch.

venues.name: Fokos Beach
venues.note: One of the last wild, unspoilt beaches on Mykonos, remote, wind-brushed and gloriously empty, with a single well-loved taverna at the back. The island's answer to those who've had enough of the scene and want silence.

venues.name: Panormos Beach
venues.note: A long, handsome north-coast bay that mixes an undeveloped stretch with the stylish Principote beach club at one end. Fewer crowds than the south coast, with an effortless bohemian-chic mood by day.

venues.name: Nammos Beach Club
venues.note: The most famous beach club in the Mediterranean, on Psarou sand, a legendary scene of magnums, designer boutiques and celebrity-watching, with genuinely excellent seafood. The apex of Mykonos see-and-be-seen; reserve weeks ahead in high summer.

venues.name: Scorpios
venues.note: The island's most-referenced beach club, on a headland at Paraga, less about wild partying and more about a curated 'music, movement and community' ritual that builds into a sunset ceremony. Bohemian-luxe and unforgettable; book day beds far ahead.
credentials: Operated by Soho House / Soho Roc House, the island's defining beach-club-to-party institution

venues.name: Principote
venues.note: The chic beach club on Panormos, striking a balance between glamour and relaxed comfort away from the south-coast intensity. Stylish loungers, good food and a calmer, more elegant scene, a fine choice for couples.
credentials: Renowned Panormos beach club, among the most prestigious in the Cyclades

venues.name: Delos Archaeological Site
venues.note: The sacred birthplace of Apollo and Artemis, a uninhabited island 30 minutes by boat, an entire Greco-Roman city frozen in stone, from the Terrace of the Lions to the mosaic-floored House of Dionysos. The essential half-day of Mykonos; hire a private guide and go early before the heat.
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Delos

venues.name: Archaeological Museum of Delos
venues.note: The on-site museum housing the finest sculpture and mosaics recovered from Delos, including the original Naxian lions moved indoors for protection. A cool, essential stop that brings the ruins outside back to life.
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Delos

venues.name: Private Catamaran Day Cruise
venues.note: The definitive Mykonos indulgence, a full day on a private catamaran or motor yacht, sailing past Delos to swim in the aquamarine coves of Rhenia, with a chef, a crew and no one else aboard. Perfect for a honeymoon, a milestone or a family day at sea; veg and dietary menus arranged on request.

venues.name: Rhenia Island
venues.note: The uninhabited sister-island beside Delos, ringed with empty white-sand coves and impossibly clear water, reachable only by boat. The reward at the heart of a private cruise: swimming and snorkelling in near-total solitude.

venues.name: Watersports & Diving
venues.note: The organised south-coast beaches, Platis Gialos, Elia, Paradise, offer everything from jet-skis and paddleboards to scuba diving over clear reefs. Easy, well-run fun for active families and teenagers between the sunbathing.

venues.name: Kiki's Tavern, Agios Sostis
venues.note: A cult taverna above quiet Agios Sostis with no electricity, no phone and no reservations, everything grilled over charcoal, the salads famous, the queue part of the ritual. A gloriously unpretentious island lunch that money genuinely can't fast-track.

venues.name: Kounelas Fish Tavern
venues.note: A long-standing family fish taverna in the back lanes of Chora, where the day's catch is chosen at the counter and the louza and grilled seafood are the real thing. The kind of honest, atmospheric table locals still keep for themselves.

venues.name: M-eating Restaurant
venues.note: A refined Chora restaurant championing Greek produce done with modern polish, a strong place to taste island specialities like kopanisti cheese in an elegant setting. Intimate and well-suited to a quieter celebration dinner.

venues.name: Interni Restaurant
venues.note: A design-led courtyard restaurant in the old town, mixing Mediterranean and Asian technique with Greek produce, that turns into a buzzing scene as the night goes on. Dinner and glamour in one; the tuna tartare and lobster are the signatures.
credentials: Long-running Chora landmark (est. 2000), the original dinner-to-party destination in Mykonos Town

venues.name: Bill & Coo Fine Dining
venues.note: The acclaimed dining rooms of the Relais & Chateaux Bill & Coo hotel, from the refined YEVO tasting menu to Beefbar on the coast, some of the most polished cooking on the island. A destination dinner for a special occasion, overlooking the bay.
credentials: Relais & Chateaux hotel dining

venues.name: Local Flavours, Kopanisti & Louza
venues.note: Two things to eat before you leave: kopanisti, the peppery, tangy Mykonian cheese spread on rusk, and louza, the island's cinnamon-and-pepper cured pork, Mykonos's answer to prosciutto. Ask any good taverna, they are the true taste of the island beneath the glamour.

venues.name: Cavo Paradiso
venues.note: The clifftop superclub above Paradise Beach that brings the world's top DJs to Mykonos every summer, dancing under the stars until dawn. The pinnacle of the island's legendary nightlife, framed here as the scene for those who want it.
credentials: DJ Mag Top 100 Clubs, ranked worldwide (2024, 2025, 2026)

venues.name: Fokos & the Wild North Tavernas
venues.note: The rugged, taverna-dotted north coast, Fokos, Ftelia, Agios Sostis, where a rough drive rewards you with empty beaches and slow, sea-facing lunches. The antidote to the port: this is where Mykonos still feels like a real Cycladic island.

venues.name: Day Trip to Tinos
venues.note: The neighbouring island 20-30 minutes by ferry, its famous pilgrimage church, marble-carving villages, wild artichokes and its own louza make it the best-value escape in the Cyclades. A quiet, devotional, deeply Greek counterpoint to Mykonos's shine.

venues.name: Scorpios
venues.note: The island's most influential day-to-night beach club, a Soho House-run temple of long lunches, ritual sunsets and world-class DJs on the rocks above Paraga, part beach club, part cultural marketplace.
credentials: Operated by Soho House / Soho Roc House, the island's defining beach-club-to-party institution

venues.name: Nammos
venues.note: The global byword for Mykonos beach glamour, a Psarou institution since 2003 that grew from a beach taverna into one of the most famous, and most expensive, beach clubs in the world.
credentials: Internationally renowned Psarou beach club, the island's most famous; a global luxury-lifestyle brand

venues.name: Principote
venues.note: A bohemian-luxe beach club on quieter Panormos, hand-crafted design, Mediterranean cooking and DJ-led afternoons that build into celebratory sunset parties.
credentials: Renowned Panormos beach club, among the most prestigious in the Cyclades

venues.name: SantAnna Mykonos
venues.note: The island's largest beach club, built around the biggest saltwater pool in Europe, an amphitheatre of daybeds, restaurants and stage shows on Paraga.
credentials: The largest beach club on Mykonos; home to Europe's largest saltwater pool

venues.name: Cavo Paradiso
venues.note: Mykonos's legendary open-air superclub, a clifftop dancefloor above the Aegean that has hosted the world's biggest electronic names since 1993, and the island's one internationally ranked club.
credentials: DJ Mag Top 100 Clubs, ranked worldwide (2024, 2025, 2026)

venues.name: Bonbonniere
venues.note: The glossy town nightclub of the Mykonos jet set, sister to London's Bonbonniere, a small, high-energy room known for star DJs, celebrity nights and theatrical champagne service.
credentials: Sister club to Bonbonniere London, a leading Mykonos Town nightclub

venues.name: VOID Mykonos
venues.note: A three-level house-and-techno club in town, one of the island's largest indoor clubs, with a music-first programme that draws a serious dance crowd.
credentials: One of the largest nightclubs in Mykonos Town, a leading house/techno venue
